connectors.note: THE READ ARROW. LAW 40's letter governs two or more arrows into ONE target and this video sends one arrow into each of TWO different targets, so the letter does not bind - the ends are built with the law's own helper anyway, because hand-placed ends are the defect the law exists to stop. anchor_points(CURSOR_BOX, 2, 'right', 0.16) and anchor_points(WS_BOX, 2, 'left', 0.16) return the SAME pair of y values on their own facing edges, so the two arrows are LEVEL to 0.00 px with each other and mirror-symmetric about the tiles' own centre axis; assert_geometry() re-derives both and refuses a mismatch. The read arrow leaves the Workspace tile's left edge on the upper anchor and lands its open chevron on the Cursor tile's right edge, terminating AT the virtual rectangle and never on top of it (LAW 7). Its ink box is the CHEVRON's extent (+/-16 px), never the shaft's. Declare data-connect-to="cursor-tile" and data-overlap-ok (a connector is supposed to touch what it joins). It crosses no printed type at any point: nothing is written in the band it occupies.

THE WRITE ARROW, the exact mirror on the lower anchor pair: it leaves the Cursor tile's right edge and lands on the Workspace tile's left edge, drawn on 'write' (5.239). Same helper, same inset, same 0.00 px level, same open chevron, same ink-box rule. Declare data-connect-to="ws-tile" and data-overlap-ok. NOTE FOR ANY LANE RE-DERIVING THESE: with n = 2 the helper's fractions are 0.16 and 0.84, which on a 112 px tile give core y 293.92 and 370.08 (canvas 485.92 and 562.08) - re-derive rather than copying a number out of prose.

boards.why: LAW 43: CHAPTERS ARE THE DEFAULT, and this take is what the default is for. The script makes THREE arguments, not one that accumulates: (1) Cursor now has one direct link into your Google Workspace, and traffic crosses it both ways; (2) the Workspace it reaches is these four named apps; (3) here is the page with the switch you flip. Holding all three in one frame would need a bridge with two banks, a four-tile row and a settings card on screen together - which is the 210 u strip that produced impossibletask_whiteboard, too small to read and too full to keep drawing. Each chapter is planned to FIT its own ideas at legible scale on the whole legal surface, and LAW 41's spacing is applied PER BOARD. Both seams HAND OVER rather than blanking (LAW 45): each erase's 0.22 s fade-out overlaps the incoming object's entrance - the Gmail tile enters at 6.680 inside the 6.500 erase and is complete at 6.98, 0.26 s after the seam completes; the settings card enters at 11.620 inside the 11.460 erase and is complete at 11.90, 0.22 s after - so the visual zone's ink never reaches zero and both handovers land on a complete, nameable object inside LAW 45's 0.30 s ceiling. Because the board is chaptered, LAW 42 wants a finite t_to on every mark: all 31 are declared and the DOM emits no data-anchor at all.

chapters.why_together: ONE mechanism: a span, its two banks, and the two-way traffic across it. The bridge drawn in the first second is the thing the arrows cross at 5 s, and READ AND WRITE is the name of the shape all of it makes. Nothing in this chapter is about WHICH apps or about WHERE you switch it on.

ONE list, named four times, and it needs the whole legal surface to sit as four 112 px tiles with four names on one level row. The row GROWS and re-centres as each tile lands, so the chapter is centred on x=540 at every settled instant instead of only at the end.

ONE place: the page, its row and its switch. erase_at is the OUTRO WIPE (an opaque rising sheet), not a chapter seam - assert_zone_never_blank() must hold across it and assert_outro_clear() must find no ink authored at or after 17.319.

LAW 35 forbade falling back to google-g.svg and LAW 33 forbade a drawn substitute, so this was a procedure, not a decision. RESOLVED.

2. WHY THE KEY TERM IS 'CURSOR' AND NOT 'GOOGLE WORKSPACE'. assert_label_law requires the key term to be the FIRST type on the board, and the first nameable thing spoken is 'Cursor,' at 0.680, whose key must land inside its 1.0 s LABEL_WINDOW. Any later candidate would force CURSOR's key to precede the key term and refuse the build.

3. THE CONNECTOR ROW WRITES 'WORKSPACE', NOT 'GOOGLE WORKSPACE'. assert_label_law keys its written map by TEXT, so two rigids carrying the same string collapse and the later time wins - chapter 0's key at 3.460 would be measured against chapter 2's row text at 12.600 and fail by 9.6 s. Both strings are faithful to the transcript and the row still carries the real mark.

4. CAPTION-IDENTITY RISK on 'READ AND WRITE' and 'GOOGLE WORKSPACE'. The guard is an OVERLAP test on identical pill text and neither is expected to collide; if it fires, the lane writes the disagreement to plans/cursorworkspace_{scene,wb}_notes.md and builds the plan as written.

PHONE TEST on 'an arch bridge': bridge / arch bridge / arched bridge over water / stone bridge / viaduct / overpass all PASS under score-the-idea; a bench, a fence or a table FAILS and the fix is a REDESIGN - deepen the arch, thicken the deck, lengthen the waterline, in that order. SEALED 6/6 sure; the remedy was applied BEFORE the first read (three arches on four piers) and the waves were added after round 1 read 'arched bridge, unsure'.

SEALED at 3/6 sure with ZERO readers naming a different object across twelve reads of four drawings; the toggle grew 96x40 -> 132x52 -> 152x60 and the card gained a filled title bar. The plan's other remedy - a second, unfilled hairline row - was deliberately NOT taken: an anonymous plate in a row is LAW 29's own named defect.
